thesis: Confirmed company-disclosed catalyst: Microsoft's fiscal Q4 2026 report on 2026-07-29 showed quarterly revenue of $90.01B (+18% y/y) and adjusted EPS of $4.74 against a $4.21 Zacks consensus, with Azure passing $100B of annual revenue for the first time (+41% for the fiscal year, 43% growth in the quarter); shares rose roughly 17% on the print, which is consistent with this run's measured 60-day move of +26.6%. The figures I could read this run are the company-preferred adjusted ones — no GAAP EPS appeared in any source I read, so treat the EPS number as adjusted and unconfirmed on a GAAP basis. The strongest counter-evidence is the securities class action filed in the Western District of Washington alleging Microsoft misled investors about Azure and Copilot, filed after the 2026-01-28 disclosure that Azure growth had abruptly slowed, alongside an FTC antitrust investigation that remains open. That does not change the read, because the specific operating deterioration the suit is built on — decelerating Azure growth — has since reversed in Microsoft's own reported numbers, and neither matter has a scheduled ruling, hearing or trial date; the class action's 2026-08-11 lead-plaintiff deadline has already passed and is a procedural date, not a merits event. This suggests the disclosed cloud/AI revenue trend still supports the position.
invalidation: Azure growth decelerates again in the October quarter, or a scheduled court/regulatory date emerges that puts a near-term binary in front of the position.

thesis: Coherent reported fiscal Q4 2026 on 2026-08-13: revenue of $2.046B (+33.8% y/y) with a GAAP gross margin of 38.5% and non-GAAP diluted EPS of $1.74 ahead of consensus, full-year revenue of $7.118B (+22.5%), and guidance projecting revenue to surpass $3B by the end of fiscal 2027. Note the mixed basis in what the company published — the margin figure I read is GAAP while the EPS figure is non-GAAP, and no GAAP EPS appeared in the sources I read this run. Despite the beat the stock fell about 6% pre-market on the print, and this run measures a 60-day move of -9.8% with the price 20.0% below its 52-week high. The explanation available is valuation rather than fundamentals: the shares carry a price-to-sales ratio around 9.47x against a historical median near 2.2x, so upbeat guidance did not clear an already-demanding bar. That reading makes the recent weakness sentiment- and multiple-driven rather than a disclosed deterioration, which is exactly why this is not a high-conviction read. Separately, several plaintiffs' firms have open investigations into 2025-era disclosures with no scheduled hearing or ruling date found, an FCC proposal to restrict Chinese optical transceiver imports is a proposal rather than a completed rule, and the Chief Strategy Officer is retiring in September 2026 in what is presented as a planned transition. This suggests the disclosed operating results still support holding, but the counter-case on valuation is named and not settled.
invalidation: fiscal 2027 revenue tracks below the disclosed path, or the FCC transceiver proposal is dropped, removing the regulatory tailwind priced into the multiple.

thesis: Dell's own disclosures remain the core of the read: fiscal Q1 revenue up 88%, AI-optimized server revenue up 757% to $16.1B, a quarterly AI order of $24.4B taking the AI server backlog to $51.3B, and management raising its fiscal 2027 AI server goal to $60B from $50B alongside a $165-169B total revenue goal. This run measures a 60-day move of +17.2% with the price only 6.9% below its 52-week high. The counter-case is that the sharpest recent leg was not Dell's own news — the roughly 9.9% gain on 2026-08-12 was attributed to CoreWeave and Super Micro results, and a further move followed Lenovo disclosing a $54B AI server pipeline, so peer read-through and Dell's disclosed backlog are both contributing without one clearly dominant. The next company-specific test is the earnings report scheduled for 2026-09-03, which is still pending. This suggests the AI server backlog continues to support the position, but the catalyst that would confirm or break it has not happened yet.
invalidation: the 2026-09-03 report shows AI server backlog conversion or margins tracking below the raised fiscal 2027 goals.

thesis: Astera Labs reported Q2 2026 on 2026-08-04 with record revenue of $392.4M, up 104% y/y, beating on both revenue and earnings and guiding fiscal Q3 above consensus, with management projecting non-GAAP EPS of $1.16-$1.21 for Q3. The tape moved hard the other way: the shares fell about 12% the following session and had already slid roughly 25% over five consecutive down days in late July, and this run measures a 60-day move of -23.2% with the price 35.9% below its 52-week high. The explanations available in sourced reporting are that operating expenses rose on continued product-roadmap investment, and that the decline was a valuation unwind after the rally had already run ahead of the results, compounded by macro uncertainty and competition. That is a sentiment- and multiple-driven account of a fall that followed a genuine beat, and I could not find a disclosed fundamental deterioration that reconciles the size of the drawdown, so the counter-case is engaged but unresolved. The CFO transition completed earlier in 2026 (Michael Tate retiring 2026-03-02, Desmond Lynch appointed) is disclosed as unrelated to operations and falls outside the recent window. This suggests the disclosed growth still supports holding, on evidence that does not fully settle the price action.
invalidation: Q3 revenue or EPS lands below the guided range, which would convert the drawdown from a valuation reset into a disclosed deterioration.

thesis: LYTE is the Roundhill Photonics & Optics ETF, which began trading on Cboe BZX on 2026-08-06 with $72M of first-day volume, a 0.65% gross expense ratio and roughly 12 holdings concentrated in optical interconnect, laser and photonic-chip names tied to the AI data-center buildout. It qualified this run on a 60-day move of +12.4% and a near_52wk_high reading of 0.0000, but both are artifacts of a nine-session listing history: the script had only 8 bars to work with, and a fund's all-time high is trivially its 52-week high when the fund is nine days old, which is also why the magnitude_score is a meaningless 30000. There is no company-disclosed catalyst here at all, because a newly launched thematic ETF has no earnings, filings or guidance to disclose; what is driving it is sector-wide enthusiasm for AI optics, the same theme already represented in this account through COHR and LITE. This suggests the signal is mechanical rather than informative, and a position would add concentration to a theme the account already carries.
invalidation: not applicable as an entry case; revisit only once the fund has enough trading history for the 60-day and 52-week tests to mean something.

thesis: Corcept has a completed, company-disclosed regulatory catalyst: the FDA approved relacorilant (Lifyorli) in combination with nab-paclitaxel for adults with platinum-resistant ovarian cancer in 2026, ahead of its scheduled action date, and the company has since resubmitted its New Drug Application for relacorilant in hypercortisolism with additional analyses the FDA requested, which it expects to draw a six-month review. A marketing authorization application for the ovarian cancer combination is also before the EMA with a decision expected by the end of 2026. This run measures a 60-day move of +46.6%, the largest in the screened set, with the price 4.1% from its 52-week high, and the reported 30-day and 90-day returns of 32.7% and 136.3% line up with those disclosures rather than contradicting them. The strongest counter-evidence is that the hypercortisolism programme has already drawn a Complete Response Letter from the FDA once, so the pending resubmission is genuinely unresolved. That does not change the read, because the approval driving the move is a separate, already-granted indication that the resubmission cannot reverse: even if the Cushing's filing fails again, the ovarian cancer approval and its EMA counterpart stand on their own. This suggests an approved and commercialising product rather than a pending binary.
invalidation: the FDA issues a second Complete Response Letter and the ovarian cancer launch metrics disappoint, or the EMA decision goes against the combination.

thesis: Marvell qualified on a 60-day move of -24.6%, and the sourced explanation for the decline is sector-wide rather than company-specific: it fell 4.65% on 2026-08-10 alongside a broad semiconductor de-risking, slid with Western Digital, Applied Materials, Micron, AMD and Nvidia in a global chip selloff triggered by cautious Samsung preliminary results, took further pressure from reports that DeepSeek is building its own AI chip, and was one of the optical names dragged down more than 10% by Corning's 2026-07-28 guidance miss. The shares are reported down 37% from their prior high and this run measures the price 29.1% below its 52-week high. I found no company-disclosed event from Marvell itself in this window explaining the move — the next one is the earnings report scheduled for 2026-08-27, ten days out, with consensus around $0.93 per share. This suggests a valuation reset in an AI-linked name rather than a disclosed deterioration, but with an unresolved binary immediately ahead there is no basis for an entry here.
invalidation: not applicable as an entry case; the 2026-08-27 report is the event that would give this a company-specific basis either way.

thesis: Rocket Lab's Q2 2026 report is a confirmed company disclosure that cuts both ways. Revenue was a record $234.07M, up 62% y/y, backlog reached a record $2.36B, and the company won a $397M U.S. Space Force Flatellites contract; against that it posted a wider-than-expected GAAP loss of $0.08 per share, and management declined to reaffirm a first flight for the Neutron rocket before year end, with CEO Peter Beck saying the window for an end-year launch is narrowing while stage-1 tank production still supports delivering the vehicle to the pad in Q4 2026. Shares fell more than 7% after hours, and this run measures a 60-day move of -23.5% with the price 45.4% below its 52-week high. The $8B Iridium acquisition announced in June 2026 is not expected to close until mid-2027 and remains subject to shareholder and regulatory approval, so it settles nothing in the near term. The record revenue and the schedule slip offset each other and neither resolves as dominant, so this suggests an unresolved setup rather than an entry.
invalidation: not applicable as an entry case; a confirmed Neutron first-flight date, or an explicit slip into 2027, would resolve the open question.

thesis: SpaceX posted its first results since going public on 2026-06-12, reporting second-quarter revenue of $7.81B against roughly $6.93B expected, and Citi raised its 2026 and 2027 forecasts and reiterated a buy on the back of it; the stock closed above its $135 IPO price on 2026-08-10 for the first time since 15 July. That is a confirmed, company-disclosed beat. The counter-case is the drawdown itself: the shares closed their first day at $160.95, traded as low as $108.27, and this run measures a 60-day move of -21.0% with the price 35.4% below its 52-week high, which is entirely a post-IPO high. The available explanation is mechanical rather than fundamental — the first-day pop unwinding after the largest IPO on record raised $85.7B, against a valuation that had been floated as high as $800B to $1.5T before pricing. Because the read on the price action rests on that mechanical account rather than on anything the company disclosed, and because that $85.7B primary raise is itself a completed equity offering inside the last 90 days, this is flagged and rated accordingly. This suggests the disclosed revenue trajectory is intact while the share-supply picture is still settling.
invalidation: third-quarter revenue misses the trajectory implied by the Q2 beat, or lock-up expiry adds supply that the disclosed growth does not absorb.

thesis: SanDisk's fiscal Q4 2026 report on 2026-08-05 is a confirmed company disclosure: revenue of $8.97B, up 51% sequentially, with roughly one third of that growth from volume and two thirds from higher pricing, driven by enterprise SSD demand and revenue recognition from the QLC-based Stargate storage platform. This run nonetheless measures a 60-day move of -18.2%, with the price 24.2% below its 52-week high, so the tape and the disclosure point opposite ways and the gap needed explaining. It resolves as a sector event, not a company one: from a closing high of $2,335.00 on 25 June the stock fell 56.5% to close at $1,015.89 on 29 July, the S&P 500's worst performer that month, in a memory-wide de-rating triggered by SK Hynix guiding 2026 capex up 50% to at least $31B, Samsung's earnings, and Chinese memory maker CXMT's Shanghai debut surging over 466% on 27 July; reporting attributes the collapse to that reset and to leveraged-fund flows rather than to SanDisk's fundamentals, and the stock rebounded 26% in a single session on 30 July. Because the qualifying signal is explained by a sector-wide reset rather than anything SanDisk disclosed, the read is capped here. This suggests pricing-led fundamentals that survived the reset, on a basis that is macro rather than company-specific.
invalidation: NAND contract pricing rolls over, or the capex-driven supply response the July selloff anticipated shows up in SanDisk's own guidance.

thesis: Lumentum reported fiscal Q4 2026 on 2026-08-11 with revenue of $1,006.3M, up 109.3% y/y and described as the first billion-dollar quarter in the company's history, driven by optical components for AI data centers; Jefferies' George Notter and Stifel Nicolaus both reiterated buy ratings afterwards, citing margin upside. This run measures a 60-day move of +14.0% with the price 10.8% below its 52-week high, so the tape and the disclosure agree. The strongest counter-evidence is that Lumentum was one of the optical names dragged down more than 10% on 2026-07-28 when Corning guided current-quarter revenue to $4.9-5.0B against a $5.0B consensus, a read-through that implied the AI optical demand curve was flattening. That does not change the read, because the read-through did not survive contact with Lumentum's own numbers: its quarter landed two weeks later at more than double year-ago revenue with margin upside, so the sector signal Corning's guide was taken to send was not confirmed in this company's disclosed results. One thing worth a human's attention rather than a risk flag: this account already holds COHR, and adding LITE would concentrate further in AI optics, which risk_rules.json deliberately does not limit mechanically.
invalidation: fiscal Q1 2027 revenue falls back below the billion-dollar run rate, or the margin expansion described on the call reverses.

thesis: Cerebras qualified on a volume spike of 2.78x, and the driver is positioning rather than disclosure: reporting attributes today's roughly 16% move and 14.65M shares against a 7.04M daily average to a wave of 13F and 13G filings showing hedge funds built second-quarter stakes, including Tiger Global disclosing a new position of nearly 3.0 million shares valued at $663M, together with Morgan Stanley reiterating overweight and raising its target on expectations that core revenue more than triples by 2027. Those are analyst opinion and fund flows, not company-disclosed events. What the company did disclose reads worse: Q2 revenue of $209.9M was described as a record but is reported as having missed consensus, and the shares fell 12% on it; separately the stock dropped nearly 14% on news that its hardware powers OpenAI's GPT-15.6 Sol Ultrafast mode, a reaction I could not reconcile with the disclosure itself. Note the metric hazard this name has already produced once for this pipeline: the '$209.9M record' figure is a core/non-GAAP measure and no GAAP revenue line appeared in any source I read this run, so the beat-or-miss question is not settled on both bases. This suggests a flow-driven move on top of unresolved fundamentals.
invalidation: not applicable as an entry case; a Q3 report reconciling GAAP and core revenue would give this a company-specific basis.

thesis: AST SpaceMobile's Q2 2026 business update on 2026-08-10 is a confirmed company disclosure and it missed on both lines: revenue of $31.5M against a $35.18M consensus, and an adjusted loss of $0.77 per share against an expected $0.26 loss, with shares falling 4.42% in the session. Against that, the company launched BlueBird satellites 11, 12 and 13 from Cape Canaveral on 2026-08-05, now has 13 satellites in orbit, reaffirmed 2026 revenue guidance of $150M to $200M, and reports a backlog approaching $1.3B with beta service and 3,000 digital cells planned across the continental U.S. This run measures a 60-day move of -11.8% with the price 46.9% below its 52-week high. The constellation progress and the reaffirmed guidance genuinely offset the size of the earnings miss, and neither side resolves as dominant — reaffirming $150-200M for the year after a $31.5M quarter puts most of the burden on a second half that has not happened. This suggests an unresolved execution question rather than an entry.
invalidation: not applicable as an entry case; a third quarter that tracks toward the reaffirmed $150-200M range would settle the question the miss opened.

thesis: Corning's 2026-07-28 Q2 report is a confirmed company disclosure with a clear negative in it. The quarter beat: core sales of $4.74B, up 17%, and core EPS of $0.78, up 30%, against consensus of roughly $4.63B and $0.76 — note these are the company's core (non-GAAP) measures and no GAAP revenue or EPS line appeared in the sources I read this run. The guide did not: current-quarter revenue of $4.9B to $5.0B against a $5.0B consensus, and the stock fell 18%, its largest single-day decline since 2002, dragging Marvell, Lumentum, Coherent and AXT down more than 10% with it. This run measures a 60-day move of -11.1% with the price 36.3% below its 52-week high. What I could not settle is the other half of the move: the shares have since recovered roughly 40% off their 29 July low without any company disclosure I could find to account for it, which leaves the current price resting on a rebound I cannot explain rather than on new information. This suggests a real, disclosed guidance disappointment followed by an unexplained recovery, which is not a basis for entering.
invalidation: not applicable as an entry case; the next quarterly report would show whether the guide was conservative or the demand signal was real.

thesis: Micron's disclosed position is strong: HBM3E capacity is sold out through most of 2026, full-year guidance was raised to $31.5-$33.5B, data-center revenue grew more than 150% on HBM3E supply to AI accelerator makers, and the company has crossed a $1T valuation. Analysts have followed — Pierre Ferragu upgraded to buy with a $1,250 target and UBS reiterated buy while lifting long-term earnings expectations on tighter HBM supply and rising HBM and NAND pricing. This run nonetheless measures a 60-day move of -10.8% with the price 19.4% below its 52-week high, so the qualifying signal is a decline that the disclosures do not explain. It resolves as the same memory-wide de-rating that hit SanDisk: SK Hynix guiding 2026 capex up 50% to at least $31B stoked fears the AI capex cycle is overheating, Samsung's results triggered a KOSPI-led selloff, and the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index fell 19% in July, its worst month since 2008, with UBS and Bank of America framing it as a healthy reset rather than a structural break. I could not date the guidance raise precisely from the sources I read, so treat it as disclosed but not pinned to a specific filing. Because the move is explained by a sector reset rather than by anything Micron disclosed, the read is capped. This suggests sold-out HBM supply supporting the position on a macro-driven entry point.
invalidation: HBM or NAND contract pricing turns, or the capex expansion the July selloff anticipated begins to show up as oversupply in Micron's own guidance.
